analysis.title: GS Dunn - GS US Daily Download 4 Nov 2026
key_insights: The rotation out of AI-related stocks into non-AI areas was sharp in October: the S&P 500 low vol index outperformed by 17%, one of its strongest relative monthly returns since the Tech bubble.
AMD reported Q3 revenue of $13.4bn vs GS $13.3bn and Street $13.1bn, with non-GAAP operating EPS of $2.09 vs GS $2.03 and Street $1.95. GS reiterates Buy and expects the stock to trade higher.
AMD Datacenter revenue was $8.5bn vs GS $8.26bn and Street $8.24bn. GS says the company has line of sight to over 80% revenue growth at the company level in 2027 despite PC market headwinds.
AMD gross margin guidance of 55% is seen by GS as encouraging given the 4Q GPU ramp, and GS expects server CPU tailwinds to offset GPU ramp headwinds.

Arista Networks 3Q26 beat on EPS, revenue and margin, raised 2026E guidance (revenue +48% yoy at the midpoint) and gave a 2027E outlook of revenue growth of 38-40% yoy, gross margin of 62-64% and EBIT margin of 49%. AI revenue is expected to double to $7bn and campus revenue to reach $2bn.
GS raised its 2027/28 Arista EPS by another 10% on average to $6.13/$7.83. Expected pushback is on the qoq decline in deferred revenue and the deceleration in bookings growth.

Arista expects an additional >10GW of XPU deployments in 2027 across 10+ accelerators, which GS views as confirmation that its networks will support custom ASIC clusters. Arista also reiterated a goal of 1-2 new 10% customers by year-end.

Block (XYZ) reported a Q3 beat with accelerating Square GPV and seller gross profit and strong Cash App momentum. Cash App credit losses came in much better than feared, which GS says should remove a multi-month overhang.

Block guided to further Square GPV acceleration into 2027 and reiterated medium-term targets of mid-teens gross profit growth and 30% operating income growth. GS flags the slowdown in PBA growth to 13% and in commerce enablement volumes. GS stays Buy with the stock at 14x its 2027 EPS.
Tech led a bounce on Tuesday ahead of midterm results. Rate-sensitive pockets underperformed as the 10Y yield rose to 4.96% after the JOLTS beat (7.523M vs est 7.164M).

The GS desk rated floor activity 4 on a 1-10 scale, with asset manager and hedge fund skews roughly flat. The desk saw a more balanced two-way picture, with some Semis/AI supply now met by buy tickets, unlike prior sessions.
Meta and Oracle traded well after recent capital raises. The desk calls this a 'paper-rich' environment concentrated in AI, and says it is important to see the market absorb large issuance.

Post-bell moves: ANET +6% on 3Q growth of +59% y/y (highest since IPO), AMD +7% on better-than-feared revenue and gross margin, PCOR +13% on revenue acceleration to +19% y/y, BKNG -7% after guiding to a sharp y/y deceleration in 4Q room nights.

market_movers.rationale: Revenue, EPS and Datacenter beat GS and the Street, and guidance supports a bullish revenue growth outlook through 2027. GS expects the stock to trade higher.
3Q26 beat on EPS, revenue and margin with a raised 2026 guide and strong 2027 outlook. GS raised 2027/28 EPS by 10% on average to $6.13/$7.83.
Q3 beat with better-than-feared Cash App credit losses and Square GPV acceleration guided into 2027. The stock trades at 14x GS 2027 EPS.
Desk color: 3Q revenue of $402mn accelerated to +19% y/y vs guide of $382-384mn, and cRPO grew +29% y/y. The stock was +13% post bell.
Desk color: the stock fell 7% after hours after guiding to a sharp y/y deceleration in 4Q room nights.

sector_views.rationale: Tech led Tuesday's bounce, and the desk sees two-way flow in Semis/AI with buyers now meeting supply. October saw a sharp rotation from AI into low vol and non-AI stocks.

earnings_insights: AMD Q3 (reported 11/4, after the close): revenue $13.4bn vs GS est $13.3bn and Street est $13.1bn. Gross margin 55.9% vs GS est 56.2% and Street est 56.1%. Operating margin 29% vs GS est 28.7% and Street est 28.0%. Non-GAAP operating EPS $2.09 vs GS est $2.03 and Street est $1.95.

AMD Q3 segments: Datacenter revenue $8.5bn vs GS est $8.26bn and Street est $8.24bn. Gaming revenue $773mn vs GS est $756mn and Street est $674mn. Embedded revenue $1.1bn vs GS est $1.12bn and Street est $1.09bn. Gross margin guidance is 55%.

Arista Q3 2026 (reported 11/4, after the close): beat on EPS, revenue and margin. 2026E revenue guide is +48% yoy at the midpoint. 2027E initial outlook: revenue +38-40% yoy, gross margin 62-64%, EBIT margin 49%, AI revenue doubling to $7bn, campus revenue $2bn. GS 2027/28 EPS est $6.13/$7.83. The desk cites 3Q growth of +59% y/y.

Block Q3 (reported 11/4, after the close): beat, with accelerating Square GPV and seller gross profit. PBA growth slowed to 13%. Medium-term targets reiterated at mid-teens gross profit growth and 30% operating income growth. The stock trades at 14x GS 2027 EPS est.

Procore (PCOR) Q3 revenue was $402mn, +19% y/y, vs guide of $382-384mn (+13.3% y/y) and +16% y/y last quarter, including 2pts of growth from the DroneDeploy acquisition. cRPO +29% y/y vs +22% last quarter.
Booking Holdings (BKNG) guided to a sharp y/y deceleration in 4Q room nights, and the stock fell 7% after hours.

Earnings 11/4 before the open: MCD, NVO, UBER, CVS, EMR, DDOG, GWW, COR, CVE, MDLN, MLM, RPRX, CHT. After the close: TM, ARM, QCOM, MCK, MELI, MSI, APP, MFC, ALL, MET, AFL, EW, VMRK, SLF, RVMD, COHR, TKO.

AMD: PC market headwinds and GPU ramp headwinds to gross margin.

vol_and_positioning: The S&P 500 low vol index outperformed by 17% in October, one of its strongest relative monthly returns since the Tech bubble.
GS desk floor activity was 4 on a 1-10 scale, with asset manager and hedge fund skews roughly flat.
The desk saw a more balanced two-way picture, with some Semis/AI supply now met by select buy tickets, vs several sessions where supply met almost zero defense.
The desk described a 'paper-rich' environment concentrated in AI, with Meta and Oracle trading well after recent capital raises.
